passage: Playgroup note, Thursday, from Uma. Nikita (2 years) rubbed her eyes twice during story time and slumped against my knee. When I asked, "Sleepy?" she nodded and pointed to the nap mats. Before lunch she patted her tummy and said, "Hungry, khana." After lunch she tugged at her shorts and did a little dance; we reached the potty just in time. 👍 I'll tell her father she's starting to put words to what her body feels.

qa.q: Where did Nikita point when asked if she was sleepy?
qa.a: To the nap mats.

qa.q: What does Nikita patting her tummy and saying "khana" show she understood?
qa.a: It shows she noticed the hungry feeling inside her and wanted food.

qa.q: What could Nikita's father do at home to build on this?
qa.a: He could name her body feelings in simple words, like sleepy or hungry, and respond when she signals them.

qa.q: How might Uma's day change as Nikita names her needs?
qa.a: Uma can meet Nikita's needs sooner, with fewer meltdowns and fewer accidents. 🙂

grounding: Shows a toddler noticing and signalling tiredness, hunger and the need for the toilet.

passage: On the local bus home from the weekly haat, Aparna, two, stops chattering. She pulls at her sandal strap and whimpers, then pushes her face into Bidisha's sari. Her mother loosens the strap; a red line shows on the small foot. Aparna sighs, then yawns wide and curls up in Bidisha's lap. By the next stop she is asleep, one fist still holding a paper packet of roasted chana.

qa.q: What mark did Bidisha find on Aparna's foot?
qa.a: A red line from the sandal strap.

qa.q: Why did Aparna whimper and pull at her sandal?
qa.a: The strap was hurting and she was tired, and she wanted the discomfort to stop.

qa.q: What could Bidisha try after this trip?
qa.a: She could check how the sandals fit and plan a rest before long outings, while watching for these signals.

qa.q: What would change if Bidisha had scolded Aparna for fussing?
qa.a: The signal about the strap might have been missed, and Aparna could have stayed sore and cried harder.

grounding: Shows a toddler signalling physical discomfort and tiredness on a village bus ride.

passage: At the playground in Leeds, Tariq, nearly three, stops halfway up the climbing frame and grabs the front of his trousers. "Wee-wee," he says, climbing down fast. Fatima, his mother, takes his hand and they hurry to the cafe toilet. Back outside, he shivers and holds out his arms. "Cold." She zips up his coat. He nods, pats the zip, and runs back to the frame.

qa.q: Which word did Tariq use when he felt cold?
qa.a: He said "Cold."

qa.q: Why did Tariq climb down so fast?
qa.a: He felt he needed to wee and wanted to reach the toilet in time.

qa.q: What went right, and how could Fatima keep it going?
qa.a: Tariq named his need early; she can keep responding quickly and noticing when he tells her.

qa.q: What is it like for Fatima when Tariq can say what his body needs?
qa.a: Outings feel easier and calmer because she doesn't have to guess.

grounding: Shows a toddler recognising the need for the toilet and feeling cold, and telling his mother.

passage: I'm Neelam, Seema's grandmother. At two, Seema has started telling us about her body. This morning she stopped playing, tugged at her nappy and said, "Wet." At lunch she pushed her plate away and rubbed her eyes. "Sleepy," she whispered, and crawled onto my lap. Later she held her tummy and made a face. I checked; she needed the toilet. She is learning what her body is saying.

qa.q: What did Seema say when she tugged at her nappy?
qa.a: She said, "Wet."

qa.q: What did Seema's rubbing her eyes and whispering "Sleepy" suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she felt tired and knew she needed rest.

qa.q: How can Neelam support Seema in noticing her body signals?
qa.a: By naming the feelings back to her and responding quickly, like helping her rest or go to the toilet.

qa.q: How does Neelam see Seema's new words?
qa.a: Neelam sees them as Seema learning to understand what her body is telling her. 😊

grounding: Shows a grandmother noticing a toddler recognising and naming hunger, tiredness and toilet needs.

passage:
Tuesday: Abhinav, twenty months, whines and throws his toy car. His father Chinmay tries to play, but Abhinav cries louder.

Thursday: Abhinav whines again at the same time. Chinmay asks, "Hungry?" Abhinav points to the kitchen.

The next Monday: Before lunch, Abhinav walks to the kitchen, pats his tummy and says, "Eat!" Chinmay smiles and hands him a banana.

qa.q: What did Abhinav say on Monday before lunch?
qa.a: He said, "Eat!"

qa.q: What was Abhinav likely feeling when he whined and threw his car on Tuesday?
qa.a: He was likely hungry and upset but didn't know how to show it yet.

qa.q: What helped Abhinav connect his feeling to food?
qa.a: His father asking "Hungry?" helped him link the uncomfortable feeling to eating.

qa.q: How might Chinmay feel on Monday when Abhinav says "Eat!"?
qa.a: He probably feels relieved and happy that Abhinav can now tell him what he needs.

grounding: Shows a toddler over several days learning to recognise hunger and say what he needs.
